ground:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Asset type: production raster background strip for a horizontally scrolling post-apocalyptic Nevada highway in a tabletop game. This is scenery artwork, not a diagram.
Create a high quality wide landscape bitmap, ideally 3072 by 1536 pixels. Camera is elevated and looking down at approximately 45 degrees from horizontal, perpendicular to the road's travel direction. The road runs perfectly horizontally from the left edge to right edge. All terrain and stones are seen at this same oblique 45-degree angle, with realistic physical material textures.
Composition: across the middle and lower part of the image a very broad worn dark asphalt highway with three horizontal travel lanes, occupying about 65% of the image height, leaving generous open asphalt space for vehicle tokens. Road begins around 22% down and ends around 88% down. Faint distressed horizontal dashed paint lines and broken white road edge markings, subtle long tyre wear. Along both edges, irregular tan sandy gravel shoulders blend into dry grey-brown Nevada desert scrubland. More terrain at the top, a narrow near shoulder at the bottom. Small stones, gravel, sand drifts, brittle sparse sagebrush. Horizontal direction, no bends and no diagonal road.
Style: gritty photorealistic film/game environment, exceptionally rich believable asphalt aggregate, dusty erosion, cracks and chipped paint; subdued sun-bleached ochre and brown, charcoal asphalt, subtle desaturated olive vegetation. Sun from upper left, soft shadows down-right. Restrained contrast on playable asphalt. Abandoned, weathered, serious post-apocalyptic mood without piles of props covering the road.
Constraints: ground surface fills the entire bitmap; no sky, no horizon, no tall hills, no buildings, no cars, no people, no UI, no grid, no symbols, no watermark. Left and right edges match seamlessly for horizontal tiling; avoid distinctive large landmarks near edges. Avoid overhead 90-degree view, low side view, isometric diagonal, cartoon/vector rendering, flat polygons, black outlines and decorative gradients.
hills: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset: wide horizontal looping background panorama for the same Nevada chase scene as the reference image. The reference is a MATERIALS, LIGHTING AND COLOUR reference, not an edit target. Create a separate landscape image. Camera approximately 45 degrees down from horizontal, elevated perpendicular to a horizontal road that is below the frame. Look DOWN onto sun-bleached Nevada desert hills and the valley floor, visible rocky ridge top surfaces and eroded faces in that same 45-degree oblique camera. Composition: upper 40% distant rugged receding brown-grey ridges softened by dry atmospheric haze, lower 60% open ochre sandy valley floor with occasional small scrub, gravel and shallow dry washes. No visible sky, no horizon-to-sky boundary: terrain continues beyond the top edge. Quiet upper background, lots of open flatter ground below for overlap with the road plate. Realistic high-detail cinematic photography/game environment, sun from upper left, shadows down-right, desaturated browns and olives matching the reference. Very wide landscape, ideally 3072x1536. Left/right edges must match in ground colour and ridge elevation for horizontal looping. No road, vehicles, people, text, UI, watermark. No cartoon, outline drawing, flat vector mountains or top-down 90-degree map.
plants: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset: transparent RGBA game sprite sheet of foreground desert plants. Reference image supplies Nevada materials, warm muted palette, lighting only; not an edit target. Make a clean 2 by 2 sheet, four separate isolated assets, each wholly inside its quadrant with generous transparent gutters, no labels. Assets: (top left) a tall dead twisted Joshua tree with ragged dry foliage; (top right) a sparse brittle desert tree with forked bare branches; (bottom left) a tangled dry cholla cactus crown with believable spines; (bottom right) wind-broken dry sagebrush and long stalks. Camera elevated at approximately 45 degrees downward from horizontal, showing upper surfaces as well as sides, same view as the reference environment. Serious gritty photographic/game-asset realism, bark fissures, brittle leaves, natural irregular silhouettes; sun from upper left and shaded lower-right faces. Neutral dry grey-brown and desaturated olive, no green lushness. Objects will pass close to the camera in front of a road; render detailed upper portions and extending trunks/stems, but NO visible roots, feet, pot, soil patch, rock support or ground-contact shadow. Lower stems simply continue out of each cutout bottom. TRUE TRANSPARENT background, no backdrop, no checkerboard painted into the image, no halo, no text, no cartoon, no outlines. Ideally 2048x2048.
structures: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset: transparent RGBA game sprite sheet of FOUR sparse roadside upper structures for a Nevada post-apocalyptic highway. Reference supplies gritty materials, light direction, muted palette only; not an edit target. Clean 2 by 2 sheet, four distinct isolated cutouts entirely within their quadrants with generous transparent gutters, no text labels. Top left: battered rusted octagonal roadside sign and partial long metal post, sign face blank with peeling faded red paint; top right: jagged broken wooden utility crossarm with short hanging scraps of wire and partial weathered pole; bottom left: upper corner of a ruined roadside wooden shack, broken sloped sheet-metal roof and jagged splintered beams, just the roof and upper wall corner; bottom right: bent rusted steel road sign frame with blank weathered rectangular plate and partial post. Camera looking DOWN at about 45 degrees from horizontal, showing top surfaces and suitably foreshortened sign faces and roofs; do not use a straight-on eye-level view. Detailed realistic photographic/game-asset material textures, serious and weathered, sun upper-left, shadows on lower-right faces. These will pass near the camera, with lower structures hidden below the frame: no feet, bases, soil, debris piles or ground/contact shadows. Real alpha transparency, no background, no checkerboard painted into image, no fringe/halo, no brand/text/watermark, no vector outlines or cartoons. Ideally 2048x2048.
dust: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset: transparent RGBA game sprite sheet of windblown Nevada desert dust, matched to the reference ground. Reference is material/colour/light reference, not an edit target. Four separate, subtle wisps of pale tan granular sand in a clean 2 by 2 sheet, each isolated in its quadrant with generous transparent margins. Thin dusty horizontal streaks and irregular sparse drifting grains, low dense cloud volume, like sand skimming just above a hot road. Camera elevated looking downward at approximately 45 degrees, so flattened dust shapes follow the horizontal ground plane; wind runs right to left. Photographic fine particulate detail, warm subdued tan, naturally feathered translucent edges. True alpha transparency; mostly transparent image, no opaque rectangle, no ground, no soil patch, no objects, no circular icons, no bold particles, no smoke column, no text, no checkerboard backdrop.
dustEdit: Edit target: the attached dust sprite sheet. Change only the contents of the four dust wisps: remove every solid pebble, ground surface, tire track and ground patch. Replace them with sparse genuinely airborne fine sand grains and soft translucent tan dust filaments floating above empty space. Keep the four separate wisps in the same 2 by 2 arrangement, horizontal wind direction and approximately 45 degree downward camera angle. These are atmospheric drifting particulate effects, NOT cutouts of dirt lying on the ground. Preserve genuine alpha transparency, including semitransparent interior. Wisps should look delicate and mostly transparent, no dense solid cloud, no backdrop, no text.
